description.fun: Burmy never goes out without its cloak. It wraps itself in leaves, sand or even household dust and rubbish, depending on where it last battled, and if the cloak gets damaged it patches it straight away with whatever is nearby. Like real bagworm moths, what happens next depends on its sex: females keep their cloak for life as Wormadam, while males grow wings and fly off as Mothim.
description.guide: Burmy is a Bug-type bagworm Pokémon that covers itself with a cloak of leaves (Plant Cloak), sand (Sandy Cloak) or refuse (Trash Cloak), depending on its surroundings. Females evolve into Wormadam and males into Mothim.
description.tagline: A bagworm that dresses in whatever it finds lying around.

branches.text: At level 20, a female Burmy becomes Wormadam and a male becomes Mothim. A female's cloak at that moment decides its Wormadam for good: Plant, Sandy or Trash Cloak, each with its own second type, while Mothim looks the same whichever cloak it wore. It mirrors real bag moths, whose females stay in their case while the males fly away.

description.fun: When Burmy evolves, its cloak fuses with its body, so Wormadam is stuck with whatever it was wearing, leaves, sand or rubbish, for life. Each cloak gives it a different second type: Grass, Ground or Steel. Its antenna and bag may nod to Baba Yaga, the Slavic witch who flies in a mortar with a pestle and broom, and its name is simply bagworm plus madam.
description.guide: Wormadam is the female-only evolution of Burmy. Its cloak, set by the one Burmy wore when it evolved, becomes part of its body: Plant Cloak (Bug and Grass), Sandy Cloak (Bug and Ground) or Trash Cloak (Bug and Steel).
description.tagline: A bagworm madam who wears her cloak for life.

description.fun: Pebbles and rocks stud its earthen cloak and hang as chains for arms. It makes Wormadam Bug and Ground type, and it's hard enough to shrug off a Starly's pecking.
A cloak of refuse that looks like pink building insulation, making Wormadam Bug and Steel type. It blends into the scenery so well that predators pass it by.

Mothim loves flower honey but won't gather any itself. Instead it flutters about at night and raids Combee hives, which is why it's never seen around flower gardens. Its name mixes moth with him, fitting the male-only partner of Wormadam, and may hide 'nim', slang for stealing; its Japanese name Gamale sounds like gameru, 'to pilfer'.
description.guide: Mothim is the male-only evolution of Burmy, a Bug- and Flying-type moth. It has no nest and roams fields and mountains in search of nectar, often stealing honey from Combee. Its female counterpart is Wormadam.
description.tagline: A honey thief that lets the Combee do all the work.
